source.title: Latent Communication Between Language Model Agents: Channels, Alignment, and the Limits of Text

page_placements.theme: Contextual, temporal and perturbation sensitivity of SAE codes

record.tranche_reason: The study measures SAE feature identity across contextual and bare-name encodings and finds extensive feature replacement, qualifying claims that SAE features are stable units. Its SAE-channel measurements also bear on whether dictionaries recover sparse, semantically informative features, but it does not test toy-model superposition.
record.gate_note: The study cites superposition as motivation for using overcomplete SAEs, but does not test overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions, feature competition, or polysemanticity. Channel-comparison and task-level results that do not test SAE feature recoverability or feature stability are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses a pretrained Llama SAE (andyrdt, layer 23) as a measuring instrument for inter-agent communication channels. Its SAE results are checks on that instrument (a semantic-relatedness gate), the performance of its own SAE-sparse channel (probe accuracy, compression), and input-dependence of feature sets (contextual prompt vs bare concept name). None of these tests whether LLMs store features in superposition, whether an SAE recovers the model's true features, or whether dictionary features are stable or canonical across SAE training runs, sizes or models. The contextual-vs-bare-name comparison feeds different inputs, so the feature changes reflect different representations, not dictionary instability.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that their hypothesis is not supported: text matches or beats latent channels on every task type, with a 3–10 pp gap attributed to Procrustes alignment. They further conclude that cross-architecture representational convergence (Llama to Mistral, 92% top-1 retrieval) is real.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses pretrained SAEs to encode and analyze LLM activations and compares communication channels; it does not reproduce toy-model superposition experiments or measure feature-direction geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature survival is compared between contextual-prompt and bare-name encodings; the reported outcomes differ across these encoding paths.

fits_no_version.finding: For 165 concepts, SAE features activated by a contextual cloze prompt largely differ from those activated by the bare concept name: 11.7% survival, Jaccard 5.8%, SAE cosine 0.187. Lost and surviving features have similar magnitudes (2.36 vs 2.46).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature sets for the same concept depend strongly on encoding context and surface form (contextual vs bare-name input).

fits_no_version.finding: The SAE encode–decode bottleneck preserves concept discriminability (99.4% probe accuracy vs 100% dense) at 28x compression. Related concept pairs share more SAE features than unrelated pairs (Δcos +0.319).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretrained SAE reconstructions retain concept-discriminating information in Llama 3.1 8B.

record.problems: The study uses one sender model for the SAE feature analysis and does not establish ground-truth feature recovery or completeness. Feature stability is assessed across contextual and bare-name inputs, which differ in context and surface form. The text notes that the dataset covers 165 general-knowledge English concepts and that prompt variance estimates rely on only 2–4 prompts per concept.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on V4 or V5 were left out. Toy-model, polysemanticity, and one-dimensional-direction claims are not tested.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity transition or geometry.
All: no capacity or polysemanticity analysis.
Whether features are distributed across neurons, and whether an SAE recovers genuine model features. The SAE is assumed valid, not tested.
Stability or canonicality of SAE features across seeds, dictionary sizes or models, and their completeness. Not tested; only input-dependence of activations is measured.

record.verdict_notes: Superposition appears only as motivation for using overcomplete SAEs, citing Elhage et al. The SAE results are instrument validation and channel performance in a latent-communication study.

versions.untested_parts: Whether toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions store overlapping near-orthogonal directions, and whether geometry depends on sparsity.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
The study tests sparse SAE feature activity and semantic information in one LLM setup; it does not test whether features are distributed across neurons or establish ground-truth feature recovery.
Feature stability is assessed across contextual and bare-name encodings for the same concepts; completeness and canonicality across models, prompts, or other settings are not established.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

rows.baseline: About 70 active features per individual forward pass
rows.note: The authors infer that the remaining active features are not concept-specific.
rows.check: About 43 active of 131,072 features reflects the SAE's trained sparsity, not evidence of sparse model features. The ~70-per-pass figure is an SAE property, not a control baseline.

rows.check: Probe accuracy of the study's own SAE-sparse channel compared with its dense and text channels. This is the study's own method compared with others, not a test of feature recovery.

relation.reason: Superposition motivates the SAE instrument; the reported experiments evaluate communication fidelity, alignment and task performance rather than superposition or dictionary completeness, stability or canonicality.

tranche.reason: The study uses a pretrained SAE as a measurement and compression tool for communication channels. Its input-dependent feature comparisons do not test any listed superposition claim version.

source_check.notes: Table 2 uncertainties are standard deviations. Feature survival compares contextual prompts with bare concept names using the same pretrained SAE; it does not measure dictionary instability.

reader_labels.condition: Llama 3.1 8B-Instruct SAE measurements in the tested concept dataset
reader_labels.reason: SAE codes retain near-dense-channel probe accuracy and show greater feature overlap for semantically related pairs (r2, r3); these results support sparse SAE features carrying semantic information in this setup.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Contextual versus bare-name encoding of 165 concepts
reader_labels.reason: Feature identity is not stable across these encoding paths: 88.3% are lost and Jaccard overlap is 5.8%, although some features survive and the study attributes the changes to encoding context and surface form (r4–r9).
